question: to the Commission Nicolás González Casares (S&D) Subject:
Review report on Regulation (EU) 2024/1747 on the electricity market

Regulation (EU) 2024/1747 as regards improving the Union’s electricity market design set 30 June 2026 as the deadline for the Commission to review that design, assessing, among other matters, the functioning of short-term electricity markets and their potential inefficiencies, including crisis and emergency situations, the EU legal and funding framework for distribution networks, and the potential for EU-wide power purchase agreement (PPA) market platforms. That deadline has now passed, but the Commission has yet to send the report to Parliament and the Council. Taking into account the urgent need to harness the full potential of the electricity market to make electricity more affordable for European consumers and increase resilience in crisis situations: 1.
When does the Commission intend to publish the review report and, if necessary, the corresponding legislative proposal?

Will the Commission ensure that the review fully addresses the effectiveness of the current market structure, possible remedies in crisis situations and the adequacy of the existing framework for distribution networks and PPAs, as required by the Regulation?
answer: EN E- 002757/2026 on behalf of the European Commission (27.8.2026) The Commission attaches high political importance to the proper functioning of the EU’s electricity market. In this context, the implementation of the electricity market design reform adopted in 2024 is a key priority. In this regard, the Commission has already taken action on several fronts, notably through the adoption of guidance on the design of two-way contracts for difference1 and a recommendation to Member States on removing barriers to power purchase agreements and other energy contracts2. In addition, the Commission is currently finalising the report reviewing the functioning of short-term electricity markets, the legal and funding framework for distribution networks, and the potential for EU-wide power purchase agreement market platforms. The Commission intends to publish this report later this year and will ensure that the report is fully in line with the required scope defined by the Electricity Regulation3.
